output.best_reason: Version B has the most distinct voice and the most tension. Lina's lines carry character: she stands because she has been sitting all day, she refuses to put a theory "into your notebook," and she admits "I was waiting for something, though I did not know what." That last line adds suspicion without stating it. Her link to the repeater through the hairsprings gives her a personal stake, and the clock facts come up in the course of talk rather than as a checklist. Version A is close behind. Its insistence on exactness and "He was well," along with "Please write it correctly," builds real unease, and the regulator details are vivid, but its voice is a little more uniformly formal. Version C is the weakest. Its short question-and-answer rhythm reads more like a transcript, and the facts come out one at a time in a sequence that feels more recited than lived. Its "it is not evidence" line is good, but it does not offset the flatter texture.
